items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: Benny Carter Trio with Harold Mabern and Ron Carter and Roy McCurdy

ctx.x: that is. You know. So it took me two weeks before he would open up to me and he showed me, he talked to me about what he was doing, then he told me about Chris Anderson and Billy Wallace and naturally Mr. Ahmad Jamal was holding court at the Persian Lounge another harmonic genius, a true musical genius. I mean everybody knows how I feel about Ahmad and Phineas, that those are my two favorite piano players bar none, and they don’t have a problem with it, you see what I’m saying. But back to about the singers,…

Johnny Hartman, I played with Irene Reid, I had all the singing gigs from Birdland so consequently I was always on the scene. See it would be three bands. John Coltrane Quartet, Benny Carter Trio with Harold Mabern and Ron Carter and Roy McCurdy or Bill Lee and Roy McCurdy. Then I’d take a break then the Horace Silver Quintet. So that went on for years you know. So that really kind of tightened up my accompanying skills because I had expertise in playing for singers, and know how to treat this singer differently…
Yeah. And you learned a lot of different keys, too, I would imagine.
